SMTO-EML-0024 — SMTO couldn't get ready to send this email

GUID: 032d70e4-8312-5de2-b4f7-df455d6698c6
Slug: email-service-unavailable
Domain: EML · Subsystem: email-smtp

What happened

  • Something SMTO needs before sending email wasn't available, such as its store of saved settings or a Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to work on a computer). Nothing was sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open More options › Parameter Store and check that it opens and lists your saved email sender. SMTO reads the sender from Parameter Store, so email can't be prepared if the store is unavailable.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection for the Gateway this conversation uses. Email is sent through a Gateway, and SMTO stops if none is available to this conversation.
  3. When both work, ask SMTO again in the same conversation. This stopped while preparing, before any email went out, so asking again is safe once the missing piece is back.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows the email preview for approval, or the connection test returns a result from the mail server.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; the details name the missing piece (parameter_store, gateway_client or run_id).

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Email preparation stopped because a required local dependency was missing from the run context: the Parameter Store, a Gateway client that supports email operations, or the run identity.

What this means

  • A local service required to prepare the email operation is unavailable. The producer identifies the failed field or preparation stage without exposing private values.

Why this can happen

  • A required local service, parameter store or run context is absent.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the reported field, failure phase and retained receipt before choosing a correction.

How to fix it

  • Read the field in the error facts. parameter_store: confirm AOR_AGENT_PARAMETER_STORE_ENABLED is true and the store reaches the execution context; gateway_client: confirm the run has an enabled, connected Gateway; run_id: confirm the operation runs inside an owned run. Restore the dependency and prepare the operation again.
  • Restore the named local service or runtime context, then prepare the operation again.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition first. Retry only when existing execution and effect evidence permits it; reconcile an uncertain prior send.

How to verify the fix

  • The required local service is available to the operation.

What not to do

  • Do not infer an authentication rejection from local validation. Preserve the recorded execution and delivery evidence before any retry.

Technical notes

  • Do not infer an authentication rejection from local validation. Preserve the recorded execution and delivery evidence before any retry.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
